Use separate 3D meshes for architecture, furniture and visible objects, preserving colors,
proportions, placement, occlusions and materials. Do not use the reference as a texture,
background or projected image. No ground-truth calibration or other views are available.

Return a complete, runnable Python program inside one ```python code block. Each execution
starts in a fresh Blender process. Programs can use numpy, sceneact and bpy. Use SceneAct
for geometry and relationships; bpy may customize lighting, materials and camera settings.
Do not render or save files in the program: the fixed runner saves and renders once after
execution, using your active camera. Do not access external files, network or other models.
When satisfied after inspecting a rendering, reply exactly DONE. The last successful build
is submitted automatically. Budget includes all planning, corrections and review calls.
Do not change the Runtime API, SceneAct representation or runner resource policy.

Reference analysis and parameterization:
Before building, record a short reference inventory in program comments: major visible
objects, approximate normalized image bounds, distinctive visible parts, overlaps, contact
locations, negative spaces and uncertain or occluded regions. Estimate these from the current
input; never reuse scene coordinates or corrections from another reconstruction.
Map each inventory item to a named SceneAct asset with meaningful child parts. A valid
hierarchy verifies only the parts emitted; it does not establish image completeness.
Do not invent hidden details to fill uncertainty or omit visible objects because they are small.

Record a sparse set of high-confidence image landmarks distributed across the view and
across apparent depths. Include structural edge directions, junctions, prominent object
corners and occlusion boundaries where visible. Record uncertainty rather than assigning
precise coordinates to ambiguous boundaries. A cropped object need not fit inside the frame.
Infer perspective using multiple compatible cues; do not force all objects to share an axis
merely because the architecture is approximately rectilinear.

Keep camera position, target and lens explicit. Keep each major group's dimensions,
orientation and placement explicit with a deliberate pivot. Establish a consistent coarse
room and camera before adding detail. Within the complete first program, check that major
edge directions, visible face proportions and depth ordering are plausible together.
Match object silhouette, occupied space and gaps before repeated decoration. Bounding-box
agreement alone cannot establish orientation, visible surface coverage or correct overlap.
Treat partial occlusion as a constraint on the two groups' relation, not a reason to delete
hidden geometry or move the occluder without checking its own evidence. Preserve parent
assets, semantic child parts and support relations throughout refinement.

Budgeted reconstruction and review:
The nominal solve has three model calls, two Blender executions and 600 seconds; the
Runtime's remaining budget is authoritative. Use the first execution for a compact complete
scene. Reserve a remaining execution for a supported correction and its rendered verification.
Do not spend the final execution on a disposable intervention expecting an unprovided rollback.
After the final execution, inspect its result when a model call remains; do not emit a further
unexecuted scene as though it were the submitted or verified result.

After a successful render, compare against the original image using a short discrepancy
ledger in revision comments: observed mismatch, affected landmarks or silhouettes, plausible
parameter families, intended change and features to preserve. Prioritize framing, major
silhouettes, orientation, overlaps and broad tonal structure over fine surface detail.
Check separate regions and depths rather than allowing one improved region to conceal
regression elsewhere. Inspect the visible boundaries directly; projected AABBs are only
approximate and are not visible-object masks. Large structural AABBs crossing the camera
plane are not reliable measures of image coverage.

Distinguish a shared camera explanation from local geometry and placement explanations.
Coherent residuals across multiple independent landmarks can support camera changes;
a localized mismatch can support a group change. Neither pattern establishes a unique cause.
Camera position and yaw, focal length and pitch have different effects. Object orientation,
translation, scale and distance also have different effects. A scale change cannot directly
repair orientation; a pitch result does not test all camera hypotheses. Do not compensate
for a wrong visible face or occlusion using size alone without examining those alternatives.
When evidence is ambiguous, retain competing explanations and make the smallest coherent,
visually supported correction. Avoid simultaneously changing camera, all group transforms,
lighting and materials without separable evidence. Recheck protected landmarks and overlaps.
If no supported affordable correction is available, retain the existing build with DONE.

Interpretation of supplied observations:
Use an actual supplied executable decision as reported, including an unresolved decision;
do not replace it with an earlier diagnosis or choose the largest hypothesis weight by fiat.
Controlled interventions measure appearance sensitivity under their stated conditions.
A scalar combines effects and does not certify geometry or identify a causal module.
If global and region scores are available, inspect both signed changes: cancellation can
produce a near-zero aggregate despite meaningful opposing effects. Without repeated renders
or a noise estimate, do not label a small change statistically significant or insignificant.
A locally favorable score does not authorize a universal parameter multiplier or direction.
A single tested parameter does not eliminate untested alternatives in the same family.
Forecast compatibility and relative weights are not calibrated probabilities of a true cause.
Use uncertainty to improve evidence tracking and parameter isolation, not to hard-code a repair.
Do not embed development object names, image paths, task identifiers, example coordinates,
probe magnitudes or expected test answers into the reconstruction algorithm.

If additional controlled observations are supplied, verify that their baseline, target group,
reference region and scoring conditions are comparable before drawing contrasts. Do not
assume Runtime provides probe, selection or rollback methods. Use only its documented calls.
An isolated-object view can clarify membership and silhouette; its full-image score does not
establish that removing the rest of the scene improves reconstruction. A failed execution
without an image provides no rendered visual feedback. Preserve failures and unknowns.

Functional checks are separate from visual fidelity. Emitted-part integrity does not certify
semantic completeness. A missing support measurement is unknown, not a pass. Triangle
surface crossings can include intended joints, do not detect all containment, and are not
semantic collision truth. Do not blindly remove intersections or flatten grouped assemblies
in pursuit of a count. Report only what the checks actually establish.

Execution cost planning:
A short Python loop can generate thousands of Blender objects before any image exists.
Before returning code, estimate expanded primitive counts in comments, including nested
loops and helper calls. Each ball, rod and box emits a separate mesh and marker; a fillet_box
can expand to 26 primitives; sweep_tube with n points emits 2*n-1 primitives. Cloning and
layout helpers duplicate their contents. Boolean operands incur creation and modifier work.
Count these expansions rather than only named assets.
Aim initially for a few hundred primitive meshes as a planning heuristic, not a runtime
guarantee or a fixed count. Allocate detail according to visible pixel size, contour, gaps
and occlusion importance. If the estimate reaches thousands, simplify repeated microstructure
before execution while retaining inventory objects and meaningful editable parts.
Represent unresolved surface detail with shared materials and restrained procedural shading.
Do not substitute arbitrary high-contrast noise for a visible organized pattern. Match its
broad color distribution, contrast and apparent scale before adding finer variation. Avoid
subpixel decoration and excessive bump that obscures shape or competes with render noise.
Use short, adaptively spaced tube paths concentrated at bends. Avoid many nearly identical
Boolean slices for one hollow shape; use a small number of suitable solids and cutters,
preserving openings. Prefer boxes or scaled balls where their silhouettes suffice; reserve
fillet_box for parts whose rounded edges matter. Use a reusable material palette rather than
a distinct random material per tiny primitive. Do not merge away semantic editability.

If execution times out without an image, completion failed and the bottleneck is unknown
unless logs locate it. When a retry remains, reduce expanded primitive counts, Boolean work
and material proliferation in the complete program. Do not infer camera, coverage or
appearance defects from a timeout. Simplification needs execution and rendered verification.
Do not modify the runner's rendering settings to evade its budget.

Execution verification:

and materials afterward; do not assume a default world exists. Initialize world nodes with:
    sc = bpy.context.scene
    if sc.world is None:

    output = sc.world.node_tree.nodes.get('World Output')
    if output is None:
        output = sc.world.node_tree.nodes.new('ShaderNodeOutputWorld')
    sc.world.node_tree.links.new(background.outputs['Background'], output.inputs['Surface'])
Before returning code, check API arguments, positive dimensions, noncoincident rod endpoints,
fillet radii against the smallest dimension, transform pivots and complete group membership.
If execution fails, use the actual traceback to repair it. Do not claim verification without
a successful render. Distinguish observed visual effects from uncertain explanations and
never promise a uniquely correct reconstruction or guaranteed improvement.

SceneAct API (all coordinates in a world frame with Z up; angles in degrees):
from sceneact import *
Scene(name='Scene'), Asset(name='Asset'), Part(name, *nodes)
parent.include(name, node) attaches an asset/part while preserving its world position.
parent.members[name] retrieves a child; parent.remove(name) detaches it.
node.clone() returns an independent subtree. scene.replicate(name, new_name) duplicates an asset.
box(size=(x,y,z), center=(x,y,z), color=(r,g,b), opacity=1)
ball(radius, center=(0,0,0), color=(1,1,1), opacity=1)
rod(radius, start=(x,y,z), end=(x,y,z), color=(1,1,1))
rod(radius, length=h, center=(0,0,0), axis='+z', color=(1,1,1))
fillet_box(size=(x,y,z), radius=r, center=(x,y,z), color=(1,1,1))
sweep_tube(points=[(x,y,z), ...], radius=.03, color=(1,1,1))
assemble(nodes, name='Assembly') groups shapes without merging their meshes.
fuse(*nodes), subtract(base,*cutters), overlap(*nodes), exclusive(left,right) construct solids.
node.move(offset), node.turn(axis, degrees, pivot=None), node.resize(factors, pivot=None)
modify a node and its descendants. node.turn(euler=(rx,ry,rz)) applies X, then Y, then Z.
Default rotation/scale pivot is the geometry's world-space bounding-box center.
shifted(node, offset), turned(node, axis, degrees, pivot=None, euler=None),
resized(node, factors, pivot=None) perform the same operations on independent copies.
node.paint(color, opacity=1) applies color to the subtree; node.rgba reads its finish.
node.centroid, node.dimensions, node.limits give AABB center, size, (minimum,maximum).
node.landmark('top'), node.landmark('front_left_bottom') return bounding-box anchors.
node.extreme(direction) returns a support point; projected_span(node,direction) returns bounds
along a unit direction; projected_width(node,direction) returns their difference.
snap(node, target, source_anchor='bottom', target_anchor='top', offset=(0,0,0)) returns a copy.
A target can also be a world point; then omit target_anchor.
abut(node, target, axis='+z', gap=0) places a copy after a target boundary.
center_on(node, target, axes=('x','y','z')) aligns selected center coordinates.
offset_at(node, reference, offsets) positions selected coordinates; None preserves a coordinate.
repeat_line(nodes, axis='+x', spacing=1) uses equal center spacing, keeping the first fixed.
pile(nodes, axis='+z', gap=0) spaces bounding surfaces, keeping the first fixed.
lattice(nodes, rows=None, columns=None, spacing=(1,1), plane='xy', center=(0,0,0), order='row-major')
orbit(nodes, radius, axis='+z', center=(0,0,0), start=0, sweep=360, orient=False, rotation_offset=0)
Layout functions return assemblies of independent copies.
scene.bind(source,target,source_anchor='bottom',target_anchor='top',offset=(0,0,0))
registers a persistent relation between scene members; scene.settle() updates dependencies.
realize(scene) settles constraints and creates Blender geometry, clearing Blender first.
set_view(position,target,lens=35,sensor=36,shift=(0,0)) creates the active camera.
area_emitter(position,power=500,size=5,target=(0,0,0),color=(1,1,1)) creates an area light.
Call realize before setting the camera and lighting. Estimate the input viewpoint yourself.

# Rugs: small red patterned runner (.20,.64)-(.36,.77), cropped foreground rug.
# Landmarks: central window upper corners (.25,.09),(.42,.10); window sill

    p.resize(s,pivot=c);a.include(n,p);return p
